text:
Dear Dr. Miller,

Thank you for agreeing to see this 21-year-old female for further assessment. Her mother reports that beginning around six years of age, the patient developed a striking metallic, silvery sheen throughout her scalp hair. On exam today, she appeared well but exhibited notable, generalized paleness of her skin and conjunctivae. Vital signs were normal, and her cardiopulmonary exam was clear. Her abdomen was soft and non-tender; the liver span was completely normal with no hepatic enlargement, and her spleen was not palpable. 

Her past history is reassuring. She achieved all early motor, speech, and cognitive milestones completely on schedule, and her family reports no generalized developmental slowing during her school years. She completed college recently, works in accounting, and takes only a daily vitamin D supplement. Family history is negative for early-onset medical issues.

Initial laboratory studies were notable for preserved red blood cell indices and normal hemoglobin levels, with no evidence of red cell deficiency, and her platelet counts remained well within standard parameters. However, on review of her peripheral blood smear, the cytologist identified strikingly oversized, prominent granules packing the cytoplasm of her neutrophils. 

I would appreciate your insight and guidance regarding the next steps in her diagnostic workup.

Sincerely,
Dr. Marcus Vance
